route.reason: Indications for dupilumab come from its FDA drug label, not from trial registry records.

draft.text: Dupilumab (DUPIXENT), an interleukin-4 receptor alpha antagonist, is indicated for: atopic dermatitis (moderate-to-severe, ages 6 months and older, not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those are not advisable) [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:0]; asthma as add-on maintenance treatment (ages 6 years and older, moderate-to-severe, eosinophilic phenotype or oral corticosteroid dependent) [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:0]; chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps as add-on maintenance (ages 12 years and older, inadequately controlled) [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]; eosinophilic esophagitis (ages 1 year and older, weighing at least 15 kg) [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]; prurigo nodularis in adults [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]; COPD as add-on maintenance in adults with inadequately controlled disease and an eosinophilic phenotype [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]; chronic spontaneous urticaria (ages 2 years and older, still symptomatic despite H1 antihistamine treatment) [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]; bullous pemphigoid in adults [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:3]; and allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (ages 6 years and older with a history of sino-nasal surgery) [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:3]. Limitations of use: it is not indicated for relief of acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2], nor for other forms of urticaria [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:3].
